home.description: AEM-Lab (fouriersolver.com) — free online Fourier series and transform calculator. Compute Fourier series, Fourier transform, Laplace transform and solve ODEs symbolically. Exact coefficients, Laplace pole-zero analysis with complex plane visualisation, real-time graphs and piecewise function support.

calculator.title: Fourier Series Calculator with Interactive Graph
calculator.description: Online Fourier series calculator with exact symbolic results. Compute aₙ and bₙ coefficients for trigonometric series, cₙ for complex series, and half-range expansions (sine or cosine) of piecewise-defined, continuous, or discontinuous functions. Spectral analysis with amplitude and phase spectrum graphs, Parseval identity, animated graphical reconstruction with the Gibbs phenomenon, and even/odd extensions. Supports any interval [a, b].

transforms.title: Fourier Transform Calculator — Direct and Inverse
transforms.description: Calculate the continuous Fourier transform F(ω) and inverse Fourier transform f(t) symbolically. Supports piecewise functions, free parameters with interactive sliders, multiple conventions (engineering, physics, mathematics), and real-time amplitude and phase spectrum visualisation.

dft.title: DFT Calculator — Discrete Fourier Transform with Epicycles
dft.description: Calculate the DFT and FFT of sampled functions and discrete sequences. Visualise amplitude and phase spectrum, reconstruct signals with animated 2D epicycles, and analyse Lissajous figures. FFT O(N log N) for up to 4096 points with configurable normalisation.

fourierIntegral.title: Fourier Integral Calculator — A(ω) and B(ω) Coefficients

Obtain trigonometric A(ω)/B(ω), cosine integral, sine integral, and complex integral representations in exact symbolic form. Visualise the reconstruction with an interactive slider and observe the Gibbs phenomenon for discontinuous functions.

fns.title: Supported special functions
fns.intro: Beyond standard trigonometric and hyperbolic functions, the calculator recognises these signal-analysis functions in symbolic input, numeric evaluation and Fourier transforms.

u.name: Unit step
u.def: Equals 1 for t ≥ 0 and 0 for t < 0. Models the abrupt switch-on of a signal: multiply by u(t) to activate a function from t = 0, or by u(t − a) to delay it to t = a.

sgn.name: Sign function
sgn.def: Returns +1 for t > 0, −1 for t < 0 and 0 at the origin. Related to the step by sgn(t) = 2u(t) − 1. Appears in the Hilbert transform and in the analysis of causal signals.

delta.name: Dirac delta
delta.def: A unit-area distribution concentrated at t = 0. Sifting property: ∫ f(t) δ(t − a) dt = f(a). Identity element of convolution and the cornerstone of LTI system theory.

rect.name: Rectangular pulse
rect.def: Equals 1 for |t| < ½, ½ at the edges and 0 outside. Use rect(t/T) for a pulse of width T, or rect((t − t₀)/T) to shift it in time.

tri.name: Triangular pulse
tri.def: A pyramid of base 2 and height 1 — the normalised self-convolution of rect. Use tri(t/T) to scale the base to 2T. Its transform is sinc², making it useful for spectral window design.

sinc.name: Sinc function
sinc.def: Defined as sin(t)/t (unnormalised sinc). Arises naturally as the transform of rect and as the frequency response of the ideal low-pass filter. By continuity, sinc(0) = 1.
